> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/liveness/agent.json`, `packages/spec/liveness/state-counts/agent.md`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **12** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **138** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 5fd4855a9ae7c24f31070227131f2eb42037aabb` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `3c806a545d1fb64d80a46eae94dc7c77cb8c1f39` — the merge of head `ff5810c0edc194abe9d3601e3e076bcee8c2e64e` into base `5fd4855a9ae7c24f31070227131f2eb42037aabb`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 3c806a545d1fb64d80a46eae94dc7c77cb8c1f39 && git checkout 3c806a545d1fb64d80a46eae94dc7c77cb8c1f39
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 5fd4855a9ae7c24f31070227131f2eb42037aabb ff5810c0edc194abe9d3601e3e076bcee8c2e64e && git checkout -B drift-repro 5fd4855a9ae7c24f31070227131f2eb42037aabb && git merge --no-ff ff5810c0edc194abe9d3601e3e076bcee8c2e64e

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 5fd4855a9ae7c24f31070227131f2eb42037aabb
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 5fd4855a9ae7c24f31070227131f2eb42037aabb` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `ff5810c0edc194abe9d3601e3e076bcee8c2e64e`
Local-runs: none

Inputs read: card #21277 (body and all four comments: the rider 5944103492, the ruling 5945617233, the claim 5945711087, the dev report 5947870181), PR #21367 (body as it stands after the 08:07Z edit, file list, the one bot comment, the net diff against `main` at the head), the check-runs on the head (read twice, last at 08:14:38Z), and files at refs through `git show` only. Nothing was built, run or re-run.

### ① Derived judgments

Each accept-set and public-surface change the diff implies, named right or wrong against the ruling of record (5945617233, letter A) and the claim surface (5945711087).

- **Accept set, `agent.structuredOutput.format` and `.fallbackFormat`:** `regex`, `grammar`, `xml` leave `StructuredOutputFormat`; `json_object` and `json_schema` stay. **Right** (ruling A names exactly these). Mechanism is `enumWithRetiredValues` from `shared/retired-key.ts`, which exists on `main` with no production adopter before this PR; its contract (member gone from `values`, so `tsc` refuses; the parse answers the retired member with its prescription and leaves zod's own message for a never-legal value) is what `agent.test.ts` pins: seven refusal pins by `path` and `code: 'invalid_value'`, one never-legal control (`yaml`, `coerce`), one `@ts-expect-error` pin per enum.
- **Accept set, `agent.structuredOutput.transformPipeline`:** `coerce_types` leaves `TransformPipelineStep`; `trim`, `parse_json`, `validate` stay. **Right.** The pin asserts the issue at index 1 of the array.
- **Public surface:** no new export. The three prescription constants are module-private `const`s written with `//` comments; the D2 conversion is a module-private `const` added to `MAJOR_18_CONVERSIONS`; the D3 file's `export const entry` is the entries-directory pattern every other `18.*.ts` follows and is not a package entry point. The only published change is the narrowing of the `StructuredOutputFormat` and `TransformPipelineStep` types, which is the declared breaking change. **Right.** `check:api-surface` runs in `Type Check · consumer gates`, now green; `check:authorable-surface`, `check:docs`, `check:spec-changes`, `check:upgrade-guide`, `check:export-origins` and the spec `tsc --noEmit` run in `Type Check · source gates`, green. `RETIRED_KEYS_BY_MAJOR` is untouched, as `retired-key.ts` §Registration prescribes for a value (not key) retirement.
- **Leftover census (read, not asserted):** `git grep coerce_types` on the head tree outside the edited files returns zero; `structuredOutput` outside `packages/spec` hits only `content/docs/references/index.mdx` (export names, unchanged), `skills/objectstack-ai/references/_index.md` (export names, unchanged) and one comment in `packages/lint/src/lint-liveness-properties.test.ts`. On `main`, `coerce_types` appeared in no committed generated artifact other than `content/docs/references/ai/agent.mdx`, so the "four ratchets byte-identical" claim is consistent with what the tree shows. **Right.**
- **D2 conversion `agent-structured-output-refused-members-removed`** (step 18, order 55, `retiredFromLoadPath: true`, `retiredAfter: '17.6.0'`): deletes a block whose required `format` was retired (one notice), deletes a retired optional `fallbackFormat`, filters `coerce_types` out of the pipeline keeping the key (the `hook-body-crypto-hash-removed` precedent). Idempotent: a second pass finds no retired member and returns the input reference. Fixture notice count recomputed: 1 (`pattern_agent`) + 2 (`invoice_agent`) + 1 (`coerce_agent`) = 4, matches `expectedNotices: 4`; the two controls ride through. **Right.** `order: 55` is also held by `translationWidgetSubCaptionRemoved` (landed from #21257 mid-run): `inApplicationOrder` documents ties as broken by the conversion's `id`, and the two conversions walk disjoint collections, so this is the designed tie, not a collision. `retiredAfter: '17.6.0'` matches the two other 17.6.0 entries on the head and the published version (17.6.0 at head and at `main`).
- **D3 entry `agent-structured-output-refused-members-retired`** and the generated region of `migrations/registry.ts` are byte-identical; `conversionIds` names the D2 id; `surface` carries no backticks as the file's own comment requires. The `STEP18_RATIONALE` fragment at order 60 has a unique order in that list. **Right.** `check:migration-registry` and `check:doc-authoring` run in `Lint & Repo Gates`, which is still `in_progress` at this reading (the dev's local runs report exit 0; CI's word is still owed).
- **Liveness ledger:** `agent.structuredOutput` moves `experimental` to `live`, `evidenceScope: cross-repo`, `verifiedAt: 2026-10-02`, evidence quoting the cloud readers (`agent-runtime.ts#compileStructuredOutput`, `ai-service.ts#AIService.settleFinalAnswer`, `TurnGovernor.unsupportedOutput` named as a symbol), note attributing every pointer to the cloud seat's reading 5943158888 and stating that no seat in the flipping session read cloud. No `producer` field: `check-liveness.mts` declares `producer` optional, the note states the measured fact (no producer in cloud at that ref, tenants NOT MEASURED), so the row honestly joins the `--producer-gap` worklist rather than inventing a pointer. **Right.** `state-counts/agent.md` regenerated (live 21 to 22, experimental 3 to 2). `Spec property liveness` is green.
- **Describes:** `structuredOutput` drops `[EXPERIMENTAL — not enforced]` on the `guardrails` wording precedent; `fallbackFormat` states the runtime behaviour the ruling asked for; `guardrails.blockedTopics` carries the rider 5944103492 item 1 wording verbatim ("exact, case-sensitive match on the tool name, on `action_` plus the action type, or on the tool category"). **Right.** Rider item 2 (`structuredOutput.schema`) is #21289's and landed on `main`; the diff leaves that slot untouched and the regenerated `agent.mdx` shows #21289's describe as context. **Right** against the claim's "Not the `structuredOutput.schema` slot".
- **Generated reference page** `content/docs/references/ai/agent.mdx` regenerated; `check:docs` green (source gates). **Right.**
- **Claim boundaries:** no `skills/**` edit, no cloud edit, no governed surface in the file list (`Governed Surface Queue Guard` green), no edit to the `structuredOutput.schema` slot. **Right.**
- **Fixture census in the PR body (the post-push edit):** textual `it(` count 42 on `main`, 46 on the head (+1 loop, +3 standalone); the loop yields 6 at runtime, so 42 to 51 is right and the corrected sentence ("Seven refusal pins … one never-legal-value control and one type-level pin … 9 new tests") is accurate. **Right.**

Nothing in the diff is judged wrong.

### ② Semver level

- Changeset `.changeset/21277-agent-structured-output-json-only.md`: `'@objectstack/spec': minor`, summary `feat(spec)!: …`, a `**BREAKING**` banner, a FROM → TO table for all three positions, the one-line fix, the `os migrate meta --from 17` sentence (the house spelling, present in eight other spec files), the Clause-② line reading `no (narrowing)`, and one ADR-0087 marker line, `adr-0087: registered` naming both the D2 and the D3 id. Breaking-as-minor is the launch-window rule `check-changeset-no-major` enforces. **Matches what the diff publishes:** an accept-set narrowing plus a type narrowing in a released package, no widening.
- `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` is the right declaration. `scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs` defines that spelling as "NOT a widening, but breaking", and the diff widens nothing: no new export (api-surface gate green), no accept-set growth. The ledger flip is not a widening by house precedent: the flip-only changeset on `main`, `.changeset/20274-agent-guardrails-live.md`, grades `@objectstack/spec` `patch`. The claim's `Clause-②: yes` rested on premise A4 (an exported guidance constant), which the dev measured false and reported as a deviation; the gate outcome is identical either way (minor, BREAKING, ADR-0087 marker owed). The changeset names the lint rule `liveness-experimental-property`, which exists at `packages/lint/src/lint-liveness-properties.ts`.
- The PR body carries `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` at a line start (line 5), `Fixes #21277`, `Part of #20274`. `Check Changeset` (which runs `check-empty-changeset`, `check-adr-0087-registration --base`, `check-changeset-no-major`) is green on both of its runs, the second after the body edit. `Part-of PR must not also close its card` green.
- `skip-changeset` is correctly not applied: a released package publishes a change.

### ③ Boundary flags

The report's `open_questions` is empty. Every `deviations` and `out_of_scope_findings` entry and every PR-body acceptance note is answered here:

1. **Clause-② `yes` (claim) vs `no (narrowing)` (PR).** Answered above, ②: the PR's spelling is the measured one and is accepted; no rewrite owed.
2. **PR body fixture-census sentence.** Corrected in the body as it stands; verified by count (①, last bullet).
3. **No form, i18n or reconciliation-test edit; the stale `omit` row.** `packages/spec/src/system/metadata-form-zod-reconciliation.test.ts` keeps an `omit` row for `agent.structuredOutput` whose `why` cites a describe and a ledger status this PR removes; the file's own rule says such a row is stale once the key is enforced and that the offer is decided at the enforcement. The test asserts nothing mechanically about the ledger status (its omit reasons are prose), so it stays green, and no `guardrails` row ever existed, so #21280 set no precedent for the delete. Deciding the offer means a control in `agent.form.ts` (which does not mention `structuredOutput` at the head) plus the four `platform-objects` translation bundles, none of which is in the claim's file surface or the ruling's execution parameters. **Escalated, not a blocker:** the `domain:spec` seat carries a follow-up card to delete the stale row and decide the Studio offer, as the dev's report routed it. The stale `why` is a known inaccuracy in a test's prose until then.
4. **Default PR labels: none written.** Correct: the dispatch named none and `skip-changeset` does not apply.
5. **"17.7.0" in the prescriptions.** Follows precedent: the `RealtimeEventType` and `StandardErrorCode` retirements named 17.5.0 while `packages/spec/package.json` read 17.4.0, i.e. the next minor. The head and `main` read 17.6.0 with pending `minor` changesets, so 17.7.0 is the next cut under the no-major rule. If the maintainer cuts a major instead, the strings are a release-time edit. Answered.
6. **No tree-scoped absence pin.** Accepted on the value-retirement precedent; the census above found zero `coerce_types` in the head tree outside the edited files and no authored `structuredOutput` outside `packages/spec`.
7. **`action_` plus the action type.** The describe repeats the rider's wording, which quotes the cloud seat's attested reading; it is attributed, and the ledger note names re-reading cloud as the only re-attestation. Accepted.
8. **`packages/cli/dist` side-build during the local gate sweep.** Local tree state, not this diff; nothing owed here.

Gate state on the head at this record (08:14:38Z): green — `Build Core`, `Build Docs`, `Check Changeset` (2), `Check Documentation Links`, `Check PR Size`, `Dogfood Regression Gate` (1/3, 2/3, 3/3, rollup), `Dogfood Verify CLI`, `Flag docs affected by code changes`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `No other open PR may claim the same issue` (2), `No other open PR may claim the same single-writer path` (2), `Part-of PR must not also close its card` (2), `Spec property liveness`, `Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL)`, `Test Core (2/6)`, `The card this PR closes must claim this branch` (2), `Type Check · consumer gates`, `Type Check · debt ledger`, `Type Check · source gates`, `filter`; skipped — `Console Pin Gate`, `Packed-tarball smoke (opt-in)`, the second `Auto Label` and `Check PR Size` runs; **still `in_progress`** — `Lint & Repo Gates`, `Test Core` (1/6, 3/6, 4/6, 5/6, 6/6), `Type Check · workspace`.
